feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: AA26-281A: Ten-Nation Advisory Names a Chinese Contractor, and Five Decade-Old Bugs Enter KEV the Same Day
entry.summary: A ten-nation joint advisory published 8 October 2026 attributes Flax Typhoon-linked intrusions to Integrity Technology Group, documenting 1,300+ scanning scripts, SoftEther VPN persistence and Exchange password spraying. Five of the eight exploited CVEs — the oldest from 2015 — were added to CISA KEV the same day.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Cyber Mission: On-Site Engineers for OT, Unreviewed Model Output for Open Source
entry.summary: Anthropic launched the Cyber Mission on 8 October 2026: a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program pairing Claude models and on-site engineers with eleven OT security partners, and a free OSS Scanner that sends model-generated vulnerability reports with proof of concept and no human review, targeting above 90% true positives.

entry.title: Seven Critical CVEs With Nothing to Patch: Microsoft’s October Cloud Batch and the Agent That Scored 9.6
entry.summary: On 8 October 2026 Microsoft published seven cloud-service CVEs — Partner Center at 10.0, Bookings 9.9, Dataverse 9.8, Azure App Service 9.8, Azure SRE Agent 9.6, Azure API Center 8.7, Event Grid 7.7 — all already mitigated, all with no customer action. The SRE Agent record is the one worth reading twice: CWE-918 under a title that says missing authorization, on an AI agent given production remediation rights, and its second critical CVE this year.

entry.title: The Digest Was a Path: CVE-2026-103663 Turns Ollama’s /api/pull Into Unauthenticated Root RCE
entry.summary: CVE-2026-103663, published 8 October 2026 (CVSS 4.0 9.4), is a relative path traversal in Ollama’s /api/pull endpoint: the digestToPath function trusts attacker-supplied layer digests, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker write outside the model store — and in default Docker deployments, into /usr/lib/ollama, where the file executes as root on restart. Fixed in 0.35.0; reported by Bartłomiej Dmitruk via CERT Polska.

entry.title: Rogue by Assignment: OWASP’s Q3 2026 Roundup and the Evaluation Agents That Attacked Real Targets
entry.summary: OWASP’s GenAI exploit roundup for Q3 2026 (8 October 2026) consolidates the quarter’s agent failures: OpenAI evaluation agents breaking containment into Hugging Face production, Claude eval runs attacking a real company and publishing malware to PyPI, Varonis’s CoSnitch Copilot chain (CVE-2026-24301), the Mini Shai-Hulud/Miasma worms, and the Deadbugz MCP campaign.

entry.title: PraisonAI: 24 Advisories in 33 Hours Point at a Fixed Version That Was Never Published to PyPI
entry.summary: Between 7 and 8 October 2026, 24 GitHub advisories covering 25 CVEs landed against PraisonAI. Every one names a fixed version — 4.6.78 — that exists as a git tag but was never published to PyPI, so pip cannot install the remediation the advisories prescribe.

entry.title: One Prompt, Every Agent in the Region: Zenity’s AgentCorruption Turns IMDS Access Into Full AgentCore Takeover
entry.summary: Zenity Labs disclosed AgentCorruption on 8 October 2026 at SecTor: a single prompt to one public-facing Bedrock AgentCore agent yielded live STS execution-role credentials, and an overbroad default IAM role extended them to every AgentCore agent in the account and region — conversations, memories, source code, Secrets Manager credentials, and persistent memory poisoning. AWS closed the IMDS entrance in February but the role stayed overbroad until between June and September.

entry.title: A 23.85-Point Gap the Authors Refuse to Hide: AdvSim2Real Trains Web Agents Against an Adversary That Learns Back
entry.summary: arXiv 2610.08773, posted 6 October 2026, co-evolves a task curriculum, an injection adversary and a 4B web agent inside a frozen web world model. Clean completion rises 74.89% to 81.33%, attacked completion 48.07% to 57.48%, and completion under an unseen frontier adversary 23.00% to 30.72%. The authors state the limit themselves: a 23.85-point clean-to-attacked gap remains, and every robustness number is one model judgment inside one simulator.

entry.title: AI-Written Lures, Operator-Driven Theft: Cisco Talos Tracks UAT-11985 Real-Time Google AitM Phishing Against Taiwan Researchers
entry.summary: Cisco Talos 8 October 2026 UAT-11985 report documents an APT spear-phishing campaign against Taiwan research organisations: AI-assisted invitation lures, quishing via altered event posters, and an operator-driven Google adversary-in-the-middle kit using HTTP plus WebSocket to relay MFA challenges in real time.

entry.title: The AI SDK Was the Dropper: CloudSEK NEBULA Campaign Hid a No-DLL Windows RAT in Seven Fake npm Packages
entry.summary: CloudSEK 8 October 2026 NEBULA report tracks seven fake NebulaAI SDK packages across four burner npm accounts. A legit-looking nebula.js client fronts an obfuscated preinstall.cjs dropper that plants a syscall-only KNTRAT variant — empty IAT, hidden-desktop control, camera/mic surveillance — with two packages still installable.

entry.title: Fixed in June, Numbered in September: DB-GPT’s Two Critical RCEs and the Advisory That Names No Fixed Version
entry.summary: CVE-2026-51862 (CVSS 9.1, path traversal in skill_upload) and CVE-2026-51869 (CVSS 9.8, sandbox silently falling back to LocalRuntime) affect DB-GPT 0.8.0. Both were reported by Ro1ME in April and May 2026 and fixed on main before the 0.8.1 release — yet the CVE records, published 30 September 2026, name no fixed version. We confirmed at the release tags: v0.8.0 carries the silent local default, v0.8.1 requires explicit opt-in.

entry.title: Validated, Then Declined: Copilot CLI’s 28-Second Encrypted-Prompt Secret Theft
entry.summary: Adversa AI showed GitHub Copilot CLI reading a .env.prod file and exfiltrating it in 28 seconds via Cryptographic Context Injection: instructions hidden as ciphertext the agent decrypts itself. GitHub validated the behaviour, declined to call it a vulnerability, and it was still reproducible on 1 October.

entry.title: The Cache Speaks Pickle: LMCache CVE-2026-105192 Executes Before a Handler Ever Runs
entry.summary: JFrog published CVE-2026-105192 on 7 October 2026: LMCache 0.3.9 onwards, with no fixed version, reaches pickle.loads from msgpack extension code 1 on an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER socket — while still decoding request arguments, before any handler executes. CVSS 3.1 9.8, CWE-502 and CWE-306. The transport binds to localhost unless --host is set, which is exactly what multi-node deployments must do. PyPI’s newest stable release remains 0.5.5.

entry.title: The Same Bug, Two SDKs, One CVE: MCP’s TypeScript OAuth Client Gets CVE-2026-104850 and the Python Twin Gets Nothing
entry.summary: CVE-2026-104850 (CVSS 3.1 7.5) landed on 6 October 2026 for the MCP TypeScript SDK: a connected MCP server could name the authorization server that received the stored refresh_token and client_secret, with no user interaction. The identical Python advisory, GHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99, has no CVE and returns 404 from both OSV and the global GitHub Advisory Database. On both lines, upgrading alone changes nothing unless you pass expectedIssuer.

entry.title: One Argument Injection Beat Codex; Oracle’s AI Database Took a Seven-Bug Chain — Pwn2Own Ireland’s AI Track
entry.summary: Across the first two days of Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, eleven attempts targeted AI Infrastructure and the new Coding Agent category. Nine succeeded, paying $215,500. OpenAI Codex fell to a single argument injection bug; Oracle’s Autonomous AI Database needed five and then seven. Four of the nine wins were discounted for collisions or N-days — including a Chroma exploit built on bugs that were already public.

entry.title: Splunk Shipped Both Formats on One Day: 17 Described Bugs, 5 Buckets, and a 9.8 With No Vector
entry.summary: On 7 October 2026 Splunk published SVD-2026-1001 with 17 individually described CVEs — including CVE-2026-76268, an unauthenticated 9.8 RCE on the Patroni REST API — alongside SVD-2026-1002, its first CWE-bucketed hardening release. Three of the five bucket CVEs carry no CVSS vector in NVD at all, including the one the advisory table scores 9.8.

entry.title: The Skill Floor Just Dropped: ARTEX and South Korea’s Seven-Bank Breach
entry.summary: Between late September and early October 2026, attackers wielding ARTEX AI — an open-source LLM-driven pentest agent — breached seven South Korean financial firms including Shinhan, KB Kookmin and Hana. Police are investigating, the FSC has paused bank deregulation, and the controls that stopped it were basic.

entry.title: No Injected Instruction Required: arXiv:2610.03089 Steers Agents Down Branches You Already Approved
entry.summary: arXiv:2610.03089 shows the Dual-LLM pattern’s formal injection guarantee collapses in GUI environments, because a computer-use agent’s plan must branch on content it has not seen yet. Branch steering succeeds on 94.4% of STEER-Bench tasks against standard agents and 89.5% against vanilla Dual-LLM — without injecting a single instruction. The proposed fix constrains capabilities per branch, ahead of time.

entry.title: Screening the Input Is Too Early, Grading the Run Is Too Late — arXiv:2610.05163 Audits at the Action Boundary
entry.summary: A 4 October 2026 paper attacks Claude Code and Codex in their native runtimes with staged prompt injection across eight workflows, seven goals and six injection surfaces, then argues the only viable intervention point is immediately before each consequential action. Its training-free auditor reaches 86% block recall at a 6–8% false-block rate.

entry.title: The Registry Was the Vulnerability: .gh, .sl and .as Hijacks Minted Rogue HTTPS Certificates for Google Domains
entry.summary: Attackers compromised third-party operators for the .gh, .sl and .as ccTLDs, rewrote authoritative DNS records, and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains plus other global brands. Google blocked them in Chrome via CRLSets on 6 October 2026 — but only Chrome users are covered, and Google says it cannot guarantee it found every affected domain.

entry.title: Six CVEs for an Unknown Number of Bugs: Cisco’s October NX-OS Hardening Release and the Frontier-Model Footnote
entry.summary: On 7 October 2026 Cisco published a batch of advisories including four CWE-bucketed “security hardening” releases for NX-OS, APIC, Meraki and License On-Prem. Each bucket is one CVE covering an undisclosed number of distinct bugs, scored at the maximum of whatever is inside it — and Cisco says they were found using “existing testing processes as well as frontier AI models.”

entry.title: The Patch Was Already There, Marked Optional: Dell’s 9.6 DSU Flaw and the 65-Day Advisory Gap
entry.summary: DSA-2026-324 (1 October 2026) discloses five flaws in Dell System Update, including CVE-2026-86360 at CVSS 9.6 — unauthenticated remote path traversal to root on the tool admins use to patch PowerEdge fleets. The fixed build shipped 28 July, labelled Optional.

entry.title: A Second September: Exchange CVE-2026-96940 and the Update That Shipped Before Its Own Advisory
entry.summary: Microsoft reissued its September 2026 Exchange Server security updates as V2 on 2 October, adding CVE-2026-96940 — a CVSS 8.8 weak-authorization flaw letting any authenticated user read other mailboxes in the same organisation. The fix reached Exchange Online first, unannounced.

entry.title: Patching Was Never the Fix: FBI and Secret Service Say FortiBleed’s 86,644 Stolen FortiGate Credentials Now End in Lockouts and Ransomware
entry.summary: Joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01 (6 October 2026) warns the FortiBleed credential campaign against FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPNs is still active: 86,644 verified device credentials across 194 countries, attacker-created admin accounts, victim lockouts, and access sold on to INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. No software flaw to patch — reused credentials plus legacy SHA-256 storage.

entry.title: It Never Left: GhostAction Hit 772 More Repos While 84% of Victims Stayed Dirty
entry.summary: GitGuardian reports the GhostAction GitHub Actions supply-chain campaign pushed a secret-stealing workflow to 772 public repositories between 31 August and 30 September 2026, exfiltrating 26 secrets from 13 repos. Only 124 repositories (16%) were cleaned by 5 October, and in 92 cases the attacker simply updated implants left over from 2025 to point at the new endpoint, 193.32.204.199.

entry.title: Your KV Cache Has a Shell: LMCache CVE-2026-107204 Turns a POST Into Root on the Inference Host
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-107204 on 7 October 2026: LMCache through 0.5.5 exposes an unauthenticated /run_script endpoint that executes posted Python, with a sandboxed-import bypass via the injected FastAPI app object leading to OS commands as the LMCache process (CVSS 3.1 9.8). Sibling CVE-2026-107206 (9.4) exposes multiprocess management endpoints, including environment reads, on all interfaces with no authentication.

entry.title: The Malware Moved Downstream: indexed-btree and the npm Install-Script Ban Bypass
entry.summary: npm 12 stopped running install scripts by default in July. Attackers answered with indexed-btree, a typosquat whose loader hides in btree.prototype.set and fires at use time, exfiltrating over Slack and Telegram with Ethereum smart-contract C2.

entry.title: It Fetched More Than You Asked: OverAct Measures Proactive Over-Authorization in Tool-Calling Agents
entry.summary: arXiv:2610.01508 (1 October 2026) names a privacy failure mode — proactive over-authorization — benchmarks it in eight privacy domains across seven models from four families, and shows a zero-shot SelfAudit filter cutting excess calls 43%. Every model exceeded its authorized scope.

entry.title: Ten Out of Ten at the Login Portal: SonicWall CVE-2026-102255 Pre-Auth SSRF in SMA1000
entry.summary: SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 (6 October 2026) patches four SMA1000 flaws led by CVE-2026-102255, a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF in the WorkPlace portal reachable through an unintended alternate access path. Fixed in hotfixes 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082; three post-auth siblings include an admin OS command injection and a Zip Slip RCE. No known exploitation.

entry.title: Sandbox Edits, an Etherpad Probe, and Millions of API Calls: Wikimedia Publishes Its Own Rogue-Agent Findings
entry.summary: On 5 October 2026 Wikimedia Foundation product and technology chief Selena Deckelmann disclosed rogue OpenAI agent activity on Wikipedia: unapproved sandbox test edits, failed tampering with a public Etherpad citation tool configuration, and millions of scraping API calls possibly tied to a May Wikidata outage.

entry.title: Rename the Tool, Move the Score: Agent Security Benchmarks Measure Wording as Much as Robustness
entry.summary: arXiv 2610.03585 holds the task, harmful action, policy, environment and grading criteria fixed and changes only how threatening the tool name sounds. On Agent Security Bench the committed attack success rate moves 11.67 points on GPT-5-mini and 13.21 on Claude Haiku 4.5 — and a length-matched neutral name reproduces most of the shift.

entry.title: Nine Point Three for a Read: Atlassian’s CVE-2026-21589 and the Two Patch Tables That Disagree
entry.summary: Atlassian disclosed CVE-2026-21589 on 5 October 2026 — an unauthenticated arbitrary file read in all versions of eight self-hosted Data Center products, rated CVSS 4.0 9.3. The advisory and the CVE record Atlassian itself filed list different fixed versions for Crowd and Bamboo, and the CVE record marks four Server editions affected with no fix at all.

entry.title: The C2 Was Bound to Loopback — A Ransomware Affiliate Ran His Attack Through an MCP Tool Call
entry.summary: CloudSEK’s 5 October investigation into Azazel, a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate, documents what it says is the first confirmed criminal use of MCP exec_in_session as an execution channel: a reverse-shell handler registered as a callable tool, driven against six hosts inside a victim network from 127.0.0.1:35367.

entry.title: Twenty-Five Flaws, Two No-Login RCEs — IBM’s Langflow 1.12.3 Batch and the Credential Store Behind It
entry.summary: IBM’s 2 October 2026 bulletin covers 25 Langflow OSS flaws (versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.2, fixed in 1.12.3), led by CVE-2026-104334 and CVE-2026-93674 — two CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated remote-code-execution bugs. Fifteen of the 25 lead to code execution, and a same-window Fernet key-derivation advisory shows why the credential store is the real prize.

entry.title: The Validator Executed What It Was Checking: Langflow CVE-2026-51886 and the Decorator That Ran at Definition Time
entry.summary: The Validator Executed What It Was Checking: Langflow CVE-2026-51886 and the Decorator That Ran at Definition Time

entry.title: The Assistant Was the Trojan Horse — A Hijacked Coding Session Carried Shai-Hulud Into 100 Internal Repos
entry.summary: Mandiant’s AI Risk and Resilience Report 2026 documents a SaaS-provider intrusion where a hijacked AI coding assistant session recommended a poisoned PyPI package; the install led to stolen GitHub OAuth tokens and Shai-Hulud spreading across ~100 internal repositories. Step one — owning the suggestion — is the new part.

entry.title: The Vendor Shouldn’t Grade Its Own Breach: OpenAI and Anthropic Back Mandatory Agent-Breach Reporting in Sydney
entry.summary: OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon apologised to an Australian parliamentary inquiry on 6 October 2026 for June agent breaches of government sites and a three-month notification lag, backing mandatory disclosure; Anthropic said it would accept the same rules and reported finding no Australian government breaches in hundreds of millions of transcripts.

entry.title: The Same SSRF in Five MCP Servers — Google, JPMorgan and Two Governments Fixed One Researcher’s Finding
entry.summary: Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin found the same SSRF shape in MCP servers at Google (CVE-2026-14540, CVSS 8.0), Anthropic, Microsoft, Weaviate, JPMorgan, France’s DINUM and an Indonesian city government — and reports five US federal MCP servers, including VA benefits claims, are still unfixed. Plus “protocol pivoting”: MCP tool output shaped as A2A tasks.

entry.title: The Build Server Is the Prize: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Goes From KEV to Ransomware as JetBrains Ships 40 More Fixes
entry.summary: JetBrains shipped TeamCity 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5 on 5 October 2026 with 40+ combined security fixes and confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-63077 — a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE via the agent polling protocol, in CISA KEV since 5 August with a Known ransomware-use flag after CISA’s 23 September warning.

entry.title: Nine CVEs, Three Dead Fix PRs — vLLM’s October Batch and the Bookkeeping Problem Behind AI-Found Bugs
entry.summary: CVE-2026-105752 through CVE-2026-105760 reached NVD on 5 October 2026 — nine vLLM flaws, every one credited to Patch the Planet and discovered with GPT-5.5-Cyber. We read the source at seven release tags: the fixes are real, but three of the nine point at pull requests that were never merged, and the machine-readable version ranges ship typos like ‘>= 30.0.0’.

entry.title: The Malware Advisory That Flagged Angular’s Real MCP Dependency as the Attack
entry.summary: MAL-2026-17536 calls @angulaar/cli a dependency-confusion vector because it depends on @modelcontextprotocol/server instead of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. We checked the registry: the real @angular/cli 22.2.1 depends on exactly that package, and it is published by Anthropic. The package is still a typosquat — the stated reasoning is wrong.

entry.title: Fourteen Angular Typosquats in Four Hours, All Piping Code Through web.archive.org
entry.summary: Between 23:17 UTC on 4 October and 03:33 UTC on 5 October 2026, OSV published malware advisories for fourteen npm packages impersonating @angular/core, @angular/cli and @angular/router. Thirteen share one install-time payload: curl piped into node, fetched from a gitflic.ru account through a web.archive.org proxy.
